incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a validation-error zero-day (CVE-2026-20245) in Cisco's SD-WAN management software to inject commands and execute code as root, chaining it with earlier Cisco zero-days to gain the required privileged access.
incidents.impact: The seventh actively exploited Cisco SD-WAN zero-day this year; no patch or workaround is yet available, and Cisco observed limited cases where exploitation pushed configuration changes to edge devices.

incidents.victim: Russian military personnel (front-line and border regions)
incidents.vector: A previously undocumented group posed as women seeking romance or volunteers on Telegram to lure soldiers into installing 'SafeLoveStealer' Android spyware and 'SiribGrabber' desktop malware, or entering Telegram credentials on spoofed login pages.
incidents.impact: The malware steals files, photos, location and documents and hijacks Telegram accounts; an internal platform ('Kontur') stored intercepted messages tagged with military ranks, unit designations and locations, indicating battlefield-intelligence collection. Researchers did not attribute it to a country.

incidents.victim: Hundreds of criminal malware operations (Fox Tempest service)
incidents.vector: Microsoft disrupted Fox Tempest, a malware-signing-as-a-service operation that signed malicious payloads for hire so they appeared legitimate, used by an initial-access broker (Storm-3075) and many downstream actors.
incidents.impact: The takedown degraded shared infrastructure that hundreds of criminal operations relied on, simultaneously reducing capability across the ransomware and malware-delivery ecosystem.

incidents.vector: Iranian-affiliated actors manipulated internet-exposed programmable logic controllers (PLCs) — including Rockwell/Allen-Bradley and Unitronics units — at US water, energy and municipal targets since at least March.
incidents.impact: A joint advisory from six US federal agencies (FBI, CISA, NSA, EPA, DOE, Cyber National Mission Force) confirmed operational disruptions and financial losses; one IRGC-linked group paused US attacks post-ceasefire but vowed to resume, while another pledged continued operations.

incidents.victim: Check Point Security Gateway / VPN customers (dozens of organizations)
incidents.vector: A critical authentication-bypass zero-day (CVE-2026-50751, CVSS 9.3) in Check Point Remote Access VPN deployments using the deprecated IKEv1 protocol let attackers establish VPN sessions without valid credentials via a certificate-validation logic flaw.
incidents.impact: Exploited in the wild since at least May 7 against a few dozen organizations globally; Check Point confirmed at least one case where post-exploitation activity was tied to a Qilin ransomware affiliate. Customers urged to patch and audit logs immediately.

incidents.vector: WhatsApp says NSO Group deployed social-engineering spearphishing attacks, tricking users into clicking malicious links to external sites, and created test accounts and groups — in violation of an October court injunction barring such activity.
incidents.impact: WhatsApp filed a federal contempt motion against NSO and published threat indicators, urging users to check whether they were targeted across platforms. NSO's appeal of the permanent injunction is ongoing.

incidents.vector: Two Russia-aligned clusters weaponized a patched WinRAR path-traversal flaw (CVE-2025-8088) via phishing emails with malicious RAR archives that write payloads to Windows Startup locations, delivering the GiftedCrook stealer and HTA-based espionage malware.
incidents.impact: Targeted military innovation centers, military formations and law enforcement for credential/document theft and persistent cyber espionage; WinRAR's lack of auto-update leaves many endpoints unpatched nearly a year after the fix.

incidents.victim: Organizations across US, UK, India, South Africa, Switzerland (multi-industry)
incidents.vector: Phishing, malvertising and SEO campaigns impersonated AI brands (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot) — e.g. a 'ChatGPT Plus payment update' lure and an 'Anthropic AUP appeal' lure using PDF attachments and Cloudflare-gated, adversary-in-the-middle landing pages.
incidents.impact: Campaigns harvested credit-card data, credentials and authentication tokens; one ChatGPT-themed wave sent up to 100,000 emails in a single day. Microsoft stresses this is brand abuse, not compromise of the AI vendors.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS / GlobalProtect customers
incidents.vector: An unidentified actor actively exploited an authentication-bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-0257) in the PAN-OS GlobalProtect portal and gateway to circumvent controls and initiate unauthorized VPN connections.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 observed probing and a small number of successful gateway-connected events; no lateral movement identified yet. Added to CISA's KEV catalog on May 29; organizations urged to hunt for listed indicators and patch.

incidents.vector: Glassworm was a self-propagating, credential-stealing botnet that targeted developers and spread via malicious software packages, using Solana blockchain, BitTorrent, Google Calendar and VPS infrastructure as command-and-control channels.
incidents.impact: CrowdStrike, with Google and the Shadowserver Foundation, disrupted the botnet by taking down all four of its C2 channels, halting its spread across the open-source supply chain.

incidents.vector: Official Red Hat NPM accounts were compromised and used to push a malicious self-spreading worm through the official channel.
incidents.impact: The worm spreads machine-to-machine harvesting sensitive credentials to steal further confidential data, affecting dozens of backdoored packages distributed via trusted Red Hat NPM accounts.

incidents.victim: macOS users (global, Anglophone and Western European markets)
incidents.vector: Operation FlutterBridge spread the new 'FlutterShell' macOS backdoor through hundreds of Google-verified ads (placed via shell companies) disguised as legitimate apps such as PDF viewers and a podcast player; some samples were validly signed and notarized by Apple.
incidents.impact: FlutterShell uses a WebView/JavaScript bridge to dynamically run attacker logic, enabling shell command execution, file manipulation and AI-summarization-based data exfiltration; many samples had zero VirusTotal detections. Google suspended the advertiser accounts.

incidents.victim: High-value Instagram accounts (incl. Obama White House, US Space Force)
incidents.vector: Pro-Iran hackers tricked Meta's AI support assistant into linking a new email to target accounts during the password-reset flow — using a VPN IP near the target's hometown — bypassing weak account recovery; accounts with MFA enabled were not compromised.
incidents.impact: The Instagram accounts of the Obama White House and the Chief Master Sergeant of the US Space Force were briefly defaced with pro-Iranian messages; attackers also hijacked valuable short usernames. Meta pushed an emergency patch; no back-end database was breached.

incidents.victim: Pay Tel (prison phone services) — inmate records
incidents.vector: A publicly exposed cloud server with no password left more than 3.4 million scanned images accessible for at least a week.
incidents.impact: The exposed images included driver's licenses, legal documents and financial documents of inmates and others; Pay Tel has since secured the server.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a bug in a smart contract that moves assets between the Ethereum and Cosmos blockchains.
incidents.impact: Roughly $5.4 million in crypto assets was drained; the company halted trading to investigate.

incidents.vector: Hackers exploited legacy protocols in the old DxSale launchpad service to drain old liquidity pools.
incidents.impact: Approximately $7.3 million in crypto was stolen from legacy liquidity pools.

incidents.victim: GitHub repositories and developer CI/CD pipelines
incidents.vector: Threat actors used a prior Nx compromise to push a poisoned Nx Console VS Code extension (CVE-2026-48027) via auto-update, compromising a GitHub employee's device; a parallel 'Megalodon' campaign injected malicious GitHub Action workflows to harvest CI/CD secrets and cloud credentials.
incidents.impact: Resulted in unauthorized access and exfiltration of internal GitHub repositories and mass harvesting of secrets, tokens and cloud credentials across public repos. CISA is prioritizing response and urged secret rotation and workflow audits.

incidents.vector: Data-theft and extortion attack; Charter's name was listed on the ShinyHunters dark-web leak portal.
incidents.impact: Charter confirmed a security breach after appearing on the extortion group's leak site.

incidents.vector: Attackers entered via compromised credentials issued to other government agencies authorized to access land and real-estate data.
incidents.impact: Roughly 600,000 records were stolen, including real names, cadastral information and other real-estate-specific property details.

incidents.vector: The Play ransomware group claims to have stolen sensitive financial documents from MyPillow's corporate network and is extorting the company.
incidents.impact: Play claims theft of corporate financial documents; MyPillow had not confirmed the incident as of reporting.

incidents.victim: Australian MP Zali Steggall and three staffers
incidents.vector: A suspected foreign state actor breached the WhatsApp account of an independent Australian MP and three staff members, believed to be part of a campaign targeting Signal and WhatsApp accounts of foreign politicians.
incidents.impact: Compromise of the MP's and staffers' WhatsApp accounts; the March incident was disclosed in late May and remains unconfirmed in attribution.
